stem:
In a Class 7 science period in a school in Jaipur, Ritu's teacher asks the class about the stage of human life called adolescence. Which of the following statements about adolescence is correct ( )
A. Adolescence is the stage when a person is fully mature before it even begins.
B. Adolescence is the period between childhood and adulthood, generally from about 10 to 19 years, when growth and reproductive maturity develop.
C. Adolescence occurs in all animals at the same ages, so a 12-year-old dog is also an adolescent.
D. Adolescence only means growing taller during middle school and involves no other changes.

options.text: Adolescence is the stage when a person is already fully mature before it even begins.
Adolescence is the period between childhood and adulthood, generally from about 10 to 19 years, when growth and reproductive maturity develop.
Adolescence occurs in all animals at the same ages, so a 12-year-old dog is also an adolescent.
Adolescence only means growing taller during middle school and involves no other changes.

teacher.key_rationale: Adolescence is defined as the human stage between childhood and adulthood, generally about ages 10 to 19, during which growth and reproductive maturity develop; only B states this correctly. A reverses the sequence (maturity develops during, not before, adolescence), C wrongly extends a human age range to animals, and D narrows adolescence to height gain only, ignoring physical, emotional, behavioural and reproductive changes.
